title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (Longue Marche continuation, §11 and following). The page interprets, via the Fermat tower, a homomorphism that had been obtained 'by purely algebraic means' in section 11 (formula (1218), p. 695').

The groups involved:
- M = N_{1,1}^{ét} is the (arithmetic/étale) Teichmüller group of type (1,1). Its discrete model is SL(2,Z) = <rho, sigma | rho^4, rho^2 = sigma^3>, which explains the subscript rho,sigma on G.
- Its centre is mu_M = {1, omega} = {±1}.
- The quotient M~ = M/mu_M is PSL(2,Z) ≅ Z/2 * Z/3. Grothendieck notes that M~ is what he had been calling M on the preceding pages.
- On the next page, M~ is identified with the orbifold fundamental group pi_1(U_{0,3}, S_3) = pi_1(M'_{1,1,Q}), the coarse moduli line viewed as P^1 - {0,1,∞} modulo S_3.
- G_{rho,sigma} ≅ Ẑ*.S^{+∧} is the algebraically constructed target. It is an extension of Ẑ* × (finite symmetry group) by M^∧. Here M^∧ is evidently the completed rank-2 lattice H_1(U_{0,3}) ⊗ Ẑ(1), the Galois group of the Fermat pro-tower, i.e. the maximal abelian cover of P^1 - {0,1,∞}.

The passage to the quotient: Grothendieck passes to G~ = G_{rho,sigma}/mu, which is an extension of F~ = Ẑ* × S_∘ (S_∘ ≅ S_3) by M^∧. M → G~ factors through M~ → G~. He explains the role of this passage a posteriori. In G_{rho,sigma} the central element -1 acts trivially on M^∧, so the quotient group did not act faithfully on the kernel. In G~ the quotient Ẑ* × S_3 acts faithfully on M^∧ (cyclotomically for Ẑ*, by the reduced standard representation for S_3).

The argument (completed on the next page): combine this faithfulness with H^0 = H^1(Ẑ* × S_3, M^∧) = 0. These vanishings come from H^0 = H^1(S_3, M) = 0 for the root lattice A_2, which the previous page already uses for uniqueness. The extension G~ is then rigid and can be identified with the group of transformations of the Fermat pro-cover (over Q, with its S_3 symmetries). Consequently M~ → G~ is the monodromy homomorphism of a profinite cover of the orbifold M'_{1,1,Q}, namely the Fermat pro-tower.

What remains: interpret the unreduced M → G_{rho,sigma} in the same way, via the morphism of central extensions (298) by {±1}. Grothendieck leaves this as a programme on the next page.

Problem served: a geometric (Fermat-tower) meaning for an algebraically defined quotient of the arithmetic fundamental group of M_{1,1}, at the abelian level over U_{0,3}.
errors: No mathematical error visible. The page is interpretive commentary; the identification of G~ with the Fermat automorphism group relies on the cohomological rigidity stated on the neighbouring pages, which is plausible: H^0 and H^1 of S_3 with values in the A_2 lattice vanish, and Ẑ* acts through the cyclotomic character.

Notation is overloaded. 'M' denotes both N_{1,1}^{ét} on this page and the rank-2 lattice on the previous page. 'M^+' in the last line likely denotes the finite symmetry group (S^+) rather than an object attached to the group M.

ideas.what: Passing from an extension by M^∧ with non-faithful action, where the centre ±1 acts trivially, to the quotient by the centre so that the quotient acts faithfully. Together with H^0 = H^1 = 0, this makes the extension rigid and interpretable as a transformation group.
ideas.modern_name: Rigidity of extensions with H^0 = H^1 = 0 of the kernel (centralizer-free extensions); outer action determines extension

ideas.what: The Fermat pro-tower as the maximal abelian pro-cover of P^1 - {0,1,∞}, descended to the orbifold (U_{0,3}, S_3) = M'_{1,1,Q}. Its automorphism group over Q is an extension of Ẑ* × S_3 by Ẑ(1) ⊗ A_2.
ideas.modern_name: Fermat curves as abelian (and noncongruence modular) covers; Galois action on the Fermat tower
ideas.usually_credited_to: Rohrlich (1977, Fermat curves as modular curves); Ihara (1986, profinite braid groups and the Fermat tower); Anderson; Coleman
ideas.where_published: La Longue Marche (1981) treats Fermat tower themes informally; unsure about this specific statement

ideas.what: Interpreting the homomorphism SL(2,Z) (or its étale/arithmetic version N_{1,1}) → G_{rho,sigma}, defined through the presentation by rho, sigma, as the monodromy of a cover of the moduli stack M_{1,1}. The cover is the Fermat tower, with the central extension by {±1} matching mu_M ↔ mu_G.
ideas.modern_name: Monodromy of the Fermat tower over M_{1,1}; the PSL(2,Z) → S_3 ⋉ Γ(2)^ab structure
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Γ(2) and the λ-line; Rohrlich); arithmetic version in the Ihara school

deep.surprise_reason: This is a coherent interpretive page inside an unpublished long manuscript. It recasts an algebraically obtained homomorphism from the (1,1) Teichmüller group as the monodromy of the Fermat pro-tower over M'_{1,1,Q}, using faithfulness and cohomological rigidity. It stays at the abelian (Fermat) level, where the content is classical: Γ(2)/±1 ≅ pi_1(P^1 - 3 points), S_3 symmetry, cyclotomic Galois action. These were treated by Rohrlich, Ihara and others, so nothing appears new to specialists. The open thread for the unreduced extension by ±1 is also elementary.
transcription_corrections: Under M~ the marginal note reads 'noté M dans les pages précédentes' (M~ was written M on the earlier pages); the transcription's '(sous M~ : ...)' is a framing artifact.
'S_∘' / '𝔖_∘' is most likely 𝔖_3 (or a variant of the symmetry group written with a small index); F~ = Ẑ* × 𝔖_3.
In the last lines, 'de Ẑ* × M^+ par M^∧' may be 'Ẑ* × 𝔖^+ par M^∧'; the image is ambiguous.
The struck-out first word is 'Cet' → 'Les théorèmes précédents éclaircissent...'.
'(pourvu de sa composante neutre)' is uncertain; it may read '(pourvu de sa structure naturelle)' or similar.
